topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: In our office, the computers ___ by an IT company every Friday.
explanation shown to learner: The computers do not check anything: someone checks them, so passive. *every Friday* is a habit now: *are checked*.
explanation in Latvian: Datori neko nepārbauda: tos kāds pārbauda, tāpēc ciešamā kārta. *every Friday* ir ieradums tagad: *are checked*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: My grandfather ___ this cottage with his own hands in 1965.
explanation shown to learner: My grandfather did the building himself, so active. *in 1965* is past: *built*.
explanation in Latvian: Vectēvs pats būvēja, tāpēc darāmā kārta. *in 1965* ir pagātne: *built*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: The parcel ___ to the wrong address, so it came back to me a week later.
explanation shown to learner: A parcel does not send anything: someone sent it, so passive. *came back* is past: *was sent*.
explanation in Latvian: Paka neko nesūta: to kāds nosūtīja, tāpēc ciešamā kārta. *came back* ir pagātne: *was sent*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: Every summer, thousands of tourists ___ the old town.
wrong options / checks: are visited | were visited | is visited
explanation shown to learner: The tourists do the visiting, so active. *Every summer* is a habit now: *visit*.
explanation in Latvian: Tūristi paši apmeklē, tāpēc darāmā kārta. *Every summer* ir ieradums tagad: *visit*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: I ___ by a bee while I was working in the garden.
explanation shown to learner: The bee did it to me, so passive: *I was stung by a bee*. *while I was working* is past: *was stung*.
explanation in Latvian: Bite to izdarīja ar mani, tāpēc ciešamā kārta: *I was stung by a bee.* *while I was working* ir pagātne: *was stung*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: This pasta sauce is my mum's recipe. She ___ it every Sunday.
wrong options / checks: is made | was made | is making
explanation shown to learner: My mum does the cooking, so active. *every Sunday* is a habit: present simple, *makes*.
explanation in Latvian: Mamma pati gatavo, tāpēc darāmā kārta. *every Sunday* ir ieradums: Present Simple, *makes*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Choose the correct option: The writer ___ in 1999, but his books are still popular.
explanation shown to learner: *die* has no object, so it has no passive: *died*. *in 1999* is past.
explanation in Latvian: *die* nav papildinātāja, tāpēc tam nav ciešamās kārtas: *died*. *in 1999* ir pagātne.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: The fire was happened just after midnight.
wrong options / checks: The firefighters arrived within ten minutes. | The fire was put out by two in the morning. | Nobody was hurt in the fire.
explanation shown to learner: *happen* has no object, so it has no passive: *The fire happened*. *was put out* and *was hurt* are correct passives: someone did it to the fire, something hurt people.
explanation in Latvian: *happen* nav papildinātāja, tāpēc tam nav ciešamās kārtas: *The fire happened.* *was put out* un *was hurt* ir pareiza ciešamā kārta.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Which sentence has a mistake?
correct answer: Our guests were arrived late because of the snow.
wrong options / checks: The roads were cleared in the morning. | Some flights were cancelled because of the snow. | We stayed at home all weekend.
explanation shown to learner: *arrive* has no object, so it has no passive: *Our guests arrived late*.
explanation in Latvian: *arrive* nav papildinātāja, tāpēc tam nav ciešamās kārtas: *Our guests arrived late.*

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Which sentence is correct?
correct answer: This song was written by my best friend.
wrong options / checks: This song wrote by my best friend. | This song was wrote by my best friend. | My best friend was written this song.
explanation shown to learner: The song does not write: my best friend wrote it. Passive: *was* + 3rd form, *was written*, and *by* + who did it.
explanation in Latvian: Dziesma neraksta: to uzrakstīja draugs. Ciešamā kārta: *was* + 3. forma, *was written*, un *by* + darītājs.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Put the words in order.
correct answer: the rubbish is collected every tuesday
wrong options / checks: also accepted: every tuesday the rubbish is collected
explanation shown to learner: Passive: *is* + 3rd form. The rubbish does not collect anything; someone collects it.
explanation in Latvian: Ciešamā kārta: *is* + 3. forma. Atkritumi neko nesavāc; tos kāds savāc.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: When ___ your house ___? It looks very old. (build)
explanation shown to learner: A house does not build anything: someone built it, and long ago. A passive question: *When was your house built?*
explanation in Latvian: Māja neko nebūvē: to kāds uzbūvēja, un sen. Jautājums ciešamajā kārtā: *When was your house built?*

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: This hotel ___ ___ by a famous architect in the 1930s.
explanation shown to learner: The hotel did not design anything: an architect designed it. *in the 1930s* is past: *was designed*.
explanation in Latvian: Viesnīca neko neprojektēja: to projektēja arhitekts. *in the 1930s* ir pagātne: *was designed*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Our flight ___ ___ because of the storm, so we stayed another night at the hotel.
explanation shown to learner: A flight does not cancel anything: the airline cancelled it. *stayed* is past: *was cancelled*.
explanation in Latvian: Reiss neko neatceļ: to atcēla aviokompānija. *stayed* ir pagātne: *was cancelled*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: These days, in many Spanish families, dinner ___ ___ quite late, often after nine.
explanation shown to learner: Dinner does not eat: people eat it, so passive. A habit now: *is eaten*.
explanation in Latvian: Vakariņas neēd: tās ēd cilvēki, tāpēc ciešamā kārta. Ieradums tagad: *is eaten*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: The police ___ the thief two hours after the robbery.
wrong options / checks: bank: caught | was caught | were caught | catch
explanation shown to learner: The police did the catching, so active. The robbery is past: *caught*.
explanation in Latvian: Policija pati noķēra, tāpēc darāmā kārta. Laupīšana ir pagātnē: *caught*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: The first email ___ in 1971. (send)
explanation shown to learner: An email does not send anything: someone sent it. *in 1971* is past: *was sent*.
explanation in Latvian: Pirmo elektronisko vēstuli kāds nosūtīja; tā pati neko nesūta. *in 1971* ir pagātne: *was sent*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: I ___ my husband at a friend's wedding twelve years ago. (meet)
explanation shown to learner: I did the meeting, so active. *twelve years ago* is past: *met*.
explanation in Latvian: Es pati satiku, tāpēc darāmā kārta. *twelve years ago* ir pagātne: *met*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: In this café, breakfast ___ until eleven every day. (serve)
explanation shown to learner: Breakfast does not serve: the staff serve it, so passive. *every day* is a habit now: *is served*.
explanation in Latvian: Brokastis neko nepasniedz: tās pasniedz darbinieki, tāpēc ciešamā kārta. *every day* ir ieradums tagad: *is served*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: What ___ at the meeting yesterday? (happen)
explanation shown to learner: *happen* has no object, so it has no passive: *happened*. *yesterday* is past.
explanation in Latvian: *happen* nav papildinātāja, tāpēc tam nav ciešamās kārtas: *happened*. *yesterday* ir pagātne.
answer notes: was happening :: Also correct: it asks what was going on during the meeting. Not *was happened*: *happen* has no passive. :: Arī pareizi: jautā, kas notika sapulces laikā. Nevis *was happened*: *happen* nav ciešamās kārtas.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: All our bread ___ by hand in a small kitchen behind the shop. (make)
explanation shown to learner: Bread does not make anything: the bakers make it, so passive. It is how the shop works now: *is made*.
explanation in Latvian: Maize neko netaisa: to taisa maiznieki, tāpēc ciešamā kārta. Tā veikals strādā tagad: *is made*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Our teacher ___ us homework every Friday, and today is Friday! (give)
explanation shown to learner: The teacher does the giving, so active. *every Friday* is a habit now: *gives*.
explanation in Latvian: Skolotājs pats uzdod, tāpēc darāmā kārta. *every Friday* ir ieradums tagad: *gives*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Correct the mistake: My phone repaired in only twenty minutes yesterday.
correct answer: My phone was repaired in only twenty minutes yesterday. | My phone got repaired in only twenty minutes yesterday. | Yesterday my phone was repaired in only twenty minutes. | Yesterday my phone got repaired in only twenty minutes.
explanation shown to learner: A phone does not repair anything: someone repaired it. Passive past: *was repaired*.
explanation in Latvian: Telefons neko neremontē: to kāds salaboja. Ciešamā kārta pagātnē: *was repaired*. Latviski "telefonu salaboja" ir bez *was*, tāpēc, tulkojot burtiski, to izlaiž.
answer notes: My phone got repaired in only twenty minutes yesterday. :: Also correct: *got* + 3rd form is the passive of everyday speech. :: Arī pareizi: *got* + 3. forma ir sarunvalodas ciešamā kārta.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Correct the mistake: Our train was arrived forty minutes late, so we missed the start of the concert.
correct answer: Our train arrived forty minutes late, so we missed the start of the concert.
explanation shown to learner: *arrive* has no object, so it has no passive: *Our train arrived*.
explanation in Latvian: *arrive* nav papildinātāja, tāpēc tam nav ciešamās kārtas: *Our train arrived.*

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Correct the mistake: Cars aren't allowing in the city centre on Sundays.
correct answer: Cars aren't allowed in the city centre on Sundays. | Cars are not allowed in the city centre on Sundays. | On sundays cars aren't allowed in the city centre. | On sundays cars are not allowed in the city centre.
explanation shown to learner: Cars do not allow anything: the city does not allow them. Passive: *aren't allowed*.
explanation in Latvian: Mašīnas neko neatļauj: pilsēta tās neatļauj. Ciešamā kārta: *aren't allowed*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Start with *My keys*: Someone found my keys in the car.
correct answer: My keys were found in the car. | My keys were found in the car by someone. | My keys were found by someone in the car. | My keys have been found in the car.
explanation shown to learner: *Someone* says nothing new, so the passive leaves it out: *My keys were found*. *found* is past: *were* + 3rd form.
explanation in Latvian: *Someone* neko jaunu nepasaka, tāpēc ciešamajā kārtā to izlaiž: *My keys were found.* *found* ir pagātne: *were* + 3. forma.
answer notes: My keys were found in the car by someone. :: Also correct, but *by someone* adds nothing: leave it out. :: Arī pareizi, bet *by someone* neko nepievieno: to izlaiž. || My keys were found by someone in the car. :: Also correct, but *by someone* adds nothing: leave it out. :: Arī pareizi, bet *by someone* neko nepievieno: to izlaiž. || My keys have been found in the car. :: Also correct: news now. *found* in the task is past: *were found*. :: Arī pareizi: jaunums tagad. *found* uzdevumā ir pagātne: *were found*.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Start with *A lot of rice*: They grow a lot of rice in this region.
correct answer: A lot of rice is grown in this region. | A lot of rice grows in this region.
explanation shown to learner: *They* here means people in general, so the passive leaves it out. *grow* is present: *is grown*.
explanation in Latvian: *They* šeit nozīmē cilvēkus vispār, tāpēc ciešamajā kārtā to izlaiž. *grow* ir tagadne: *is grown*.
answer notes: A lot of rice grows in this region. :: Also correct: here the rice does the growing. *is grown* says that people grow it. :: Arī pareizi: te rīsi paši aug. *is grown* saka, ka to audzē cilvēki.

topic: Active or passive? Present and past
task: Start with *A boy from our street*: The window was broken by a boy from our street.
correct answer: A boy from our street broke the window.
explanation shown to learner: The boy did it, so the sentence that starts with him is active: *broke*. *was broken* is past, so *broke* is past too.
explanation in Latvian: Zēns to izdarīja, tāpēc teikums, kas sākas ar viņu, ir darāmajā kārtā: *broke*. *was broken* ir pagātne, tāpēc arī *broke*.
